title: Balanced Quinoa Harvest Salad
subtitle: with Roast Veggies and Black Beans
description: Seriously, this salad bowl tastes every bit as delicious and nourishing as it looks! There's roasted sweet potato and cauliflower tossed in Moroccan spices, black beans and quinoa for protein, plus fresh lettuce and roasted pistachios to top it off.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Cut the unpeeled sweet potato into 2cm chunks. Cut the cauliflower stem into 1cm chunks, then cut the head into small florets. Drain and rinse the beans.

Roast veggies: Put the sweet potato and cauliflower on the lined tray. Scatter over half the Moroccan seasoning and drizzle with 1 tbs olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Roast for 20 mins. Add the beans to the tray and roast for a further 5 mins or until the veggies are tender and the beans are warmed through.

Cook quinoa: Meanwhile, put the quinoa in a sieve, then rinse well and drain. Put the quinoa and remaining Moroccan seasoning in a small saucepan with 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, for 12-15 mins until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for 5 mins.

Toast pistachios: Put the pistachios in a cold small frypan over medium heat. Toast, tossing, for 3-4 mins until golden. Remove from the pan. Trim the lettuce (see Cooking tip), then thinly slice. Put 1 tbs olive oil, 2 tsp white wine vinegar, 1 tsp sugar and ½ tsp dijon mustard in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper and stir to combine. Add the lettuce and toss to coat.

Serve up: Coarsely chop the pistachios. Put the quinoa and roast veggies in a bowl and toss to combine. Divide the quinoa mixture among bowls, top with the lettuce and scatter over the pistachios. Enjoy!

Did you know?: There aren't many sources of complete protein in the plant world, but quinoa is one of them, making it ideal for those following a vegetarian or vegan diet. Although we cook and treat it like a grain, technically speaking, quinoa is a 'pseudo grain' because it's actually a type of seed.
